title: Workspace Control Throughput & CI Efficiency v1
goal: Measure and remove avoidable latency from ChatGPT/GitHub/workspace-control execution loops while preserving provenance, fail-closed mutation semantics, durable recovery, and implementation quality. Optimize both orchestration overhead and CI topology so routine low-risk changes do not pay the same synchronous validation cost as high-risk production changes, without weakening the full safety net.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an empirical latency decomposition for representative recent ChatGPT/GitHub control cycles, separating tool-call/orchestration time, Git mutation count, PR CI, canonical-main CI, status polling, runtime/human handoffs, and genuinely necessary validation.

Study documented practices from mature CI/CD and monorepo/control-plane systems using primary or authoritative sources where possible, including validation tiers, test-impact/path selection, caching, concurrency cancellation, merge queues or tested-merge semantics, pre-submit versus post-submit roles, and scheduled/full regression coverage.

Inventory the GitHub connector/tool surface for atomic or batched multi-file mutation, check-suite/status reads, pull-request/merge operations, and other capabilities that can reduce serial tool round trips without falling back to unnecessary chat-bash.

Define a risk-based validation taxonomy with at least fast/local-static, targeted PR, full integration, and scheduled/canonical regression tiers, including explicit escalation rules for schema, database, daemon, Docker/deployment, scientific-state, and other high-consequence changes.

Demonstrate that low-risk documentation/test/harness-only changes can avoid unnecessary Docker image or full PostgreSQL/integration work when dependency/production paths are provably unaffected, while high-risk changes retain equivalent or stronger validation.

Define when PR-head validation is sufficient to continue conversational work and when synchronous canonical-main CI is actually required, using verified Git tree/merge semantics rather than assuming duplicate CI is redundant.

Define an orchestration contract that batches related Git mutations before opening/updating a PR, avoids repeated CI restarts from incremental fix commits when preventable, performs useful work while CI runs, and polls status at bounded intervals rather than tight loops.

Evaluate GitHub Actions optimizations such as dependency caches, Docker layer caches, path filters, job decomposition, reusable workflows, concurrency/cancel-in-progress, required versus advisory checks, and merge-queue/tested-merge approaches against this repository's actual risk model.
Implement only evidence-supported changes and retain a simple escape hatch that forces the complete validation suite for any ambiguous or high-risk mutation.
Benchmark before/after end-to-end control-cycle latency on at least three mutation classes: trivial/low-risk, moderate code change, and high-risk integration/deployment change.
Show that the optimized system preserves task-capsule JSON/Markdown synchronization, remote checkpoint verification, branch cleanliness, authority boundaries, and fail-closed behavior.
Document the resulting execution guidance so a fresh ChatGPT/Codex session can choose the cheapest valid validation path without relying on prior conversation state.

Every fresh-chat initialization or handoff prompt for this task must include the full workspace-control repository URL https://github.com/adamtrott78/workspace-control so a new chat can initialize from the durable control plane.
constraints: Do not optimize by simply deleting tests, weakening scientific/provenance invariants, skipping required branch-state checks, or treating failed/missing CI as success.
Do not assume every duplicate-looking PR/main CI pair is redundant; prove equivalence or define the integration risk that requires both.
Do not make research-engine production/scientific behavior changes merely to benchmark CI throughput.
Prefer direct GitHub tooling and connector-native operations over human shell steps when equivalent authority and evidence are available.
Do not introduce a new external CI vendor unless the measured bottleneck cannot be addressed with the existing GitHub/workspace-control stack and the tradeoff is explicitly justified.
Do not make workspace-control main a high-frequency telemetry sink; benchmark evidence should be compact and durable.
Use real recent workflow-run timestamps and job composition as baseline evidence instead of estimating latency from subjective waiting alone.

Separate assistant-orchestration inefficiency from GitHub Actions runtime: repeated polling, serial file mutations, premature PR creation, duplicated reads, and unnecessary synchronous waiting are first-class targets.
Do not require canonical-main CI to block the conversational critical path unless the validation design proves it is needed for the specific mutation class.

Preserve a force-full-validation path for ambiguous changes and any mutation affecting database schema, daemon lifecycle, deployment/container build, security/credentials, scientific-state materialization, or shared control-plane contracts.

Keep research-engine read-only during the initial measurement/research/design stages; expand mutation authority explicitly in the capsule only if a validated implementation plan requires representative CI changes there.

inputs: recent research-engine PR/main CI run history from PaddleOCR-VL iteration
outputs: connector mutation/status capability inventory with current update_ref lease limitation

evidence: PR #73-#77 final successful pull-request runs: 73, 75, 81, 81, 91 seconds (401 seconds total; 80.2 second mean).
Corresponding canonical-main runs: 75, 65, 81, 82, 81 seconds (384 seconds total; 76.8 second mean).

The ten successful runs total 785 seconds (~13.1 minutes). PR #75 additionally consumed a failed 58-second PR run before a corrective commit, bringing observed CI consumption in the five-fix slice to at least 843 seconds (~14.1 minutes).

PR #77 log intervals: PostgreSQL pull/start ~12.0 s, health wait ~6.2 s, setup-python ~3.3 s, install ~12.0 s, pytest ~21.8 s, Compose validation ~2.7 s, Docker build ~18.7 s; compile/checkout were sub-second to ~1 s.
Main #77 showed the same dominant structure: PostgreSQL pull/start+health ~18.9 s, install ~9.2 s, pytest ~21.0 s, Docker build ~17.6 s.

validation.check: Orchestration overhead bounded from durable evidence
evidence: PRs #73-#77 contained 23 branch commits for five logical fixes; most commits were seconds apart and could be represented as fewer logical Git checkpoints.
PR #75 opened before the final correction and therefore ran a failed 58-second workflow before a second full PR run.
Exact historical connector polling count is not reconstructible because reads leave no Git/Actions record; it is retained as an explicitly unmeasured positive term rather than assumed zero.

validation.check: Tested-tree duplication verified for representative slice
evidence: For each final PR run #73-#77, the refs/pull/<N>/merge synthetic merge tree SHA exactly equaled the eventual squash-merged main commit tree SHA.
For this sample only, immediate post-merge main CI repeated the same workflow over the same Git tree; architecture preserves escalation when tree identity/equivalent merge semantics are not proven.
create_blob, create_tree, create_commit, and plain update_ref were exercised successfully to create atomic multi-file commits.

The advertised update_ref expected_sha parameter was rejected by connector input validation, so current guidance requires immediate pre-write head verification and post-write ref verification instead of claiming lease protection.
High-level run/status, job, logs, diff, PR, and failed-job rerun surfaces are available, allowing status-first and logs-on-failure orchestration.

Recent small PaddleOCR-VL fixes repeatedly ran the same repository CI stack once for pull_request and again immediately after merge on main.
Representative paired means: PR 80.2 s; main 76.8 s; five pairs total 785 s.
GitHub file mutations were frequently serialized as separate create/update commits because the current chat used file-level connector actions.
Several iterations opened a PR and then required follow-up commits, causing additional CI restarts.
The assistant repeatedly polled workflow/job state at short intervals while no state changed, adding connector round trips without increasing validation coverage.
The full CI job includes installation, compile, full tests/PostgreSQL integration, Compose validation, and daemon image build even for narrow benchmark-script/contract changes.
The conversation often synchronously waited for both PR-head and canonical-main CI before proceeding, even when the immediate next task was unrelated local runtime experimentation.
